overview: This code defines a simple pipeline for processing text documents into a vector store using basic text cleaning and tokenization. It utilizes helper functions to prepare the text and a class to manage the storage and retrieval of vector representations of the documents.

blocks.name: Library Imports
blocks.description: This block imports necessary libraries for data manipulation and machine learning. It includes pandas for data handling, langchain for OpenAI integration, and numpy for numerical operations. These libraries provide essential functionalities that will be used throughout the code.
blocks.content:
# Import necessary libraries
import pandas as pd
from langchain import OpenAI
import numpy as np

blocks.name: Text Cleaning and Tokenization Functions
blocks.description: This block contains helper functions that are used to preprocess text documents. The 'clean_text' function removes extra whitespace and normalizes the text, while the 'tokenize' function converts the cleaned text into lowercase tokens. These functions are essential for preparing the input data for the vector store.

blocks.name: VectorStore Class Definition
blocks.description: This block defines the 'VectorStore' class, which is responsible for storing and managing vectors (tokenized documents). It includes methods to add vectors and perform a simplified search. This class encapsulates the functionality needed to handle the embeddings of the documents processed in the pipeline.

blocks.name: RAG Graph Building Function
blocks.description: This block contains the 'build_rag_graph' function, which is the main function for constructing the RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipeline. It initializes a VectorStore instance, processes a list of documents by cleaning and tokenizing them, and adds the resulting tokens to the vector store. This function orchestrates the flow of data from raw documents to a structured vector representation.
blocks.content:
def build_rag_graph(documents):
    """Main function to build RAG pipeline."""
    store = VectorStore()
    
    for doc in documents:
        cleaned = clean_text(doc)
        tokens = tokenize(cleaned)
        # Add to store (simplified)
        store.add(tokens)
    
    return store
